item: An article the batched collect flush has just inserted is indexed without reading its mention rows, which would have been empty
summary: index_article read the article's stored mention rows inside the write-gate hold, one statement per article; for an article the batch inserted in the same transaction the answer is empty (a reused id met no rows: the delete cascaded under foreign_keys=ON). index_article(inserted_in_this_transaction=True), which ArticleBatch._index_one passes (that one line in src/ingest/batch.py and its test, tests/test_batch_inserted_in_transaction.py, are in the same commit as the parameter), takes the empty answer without the statement; a re-index still reads, and the flag on an article that has rows fails on the unique index instead of storing a wrong row. Stored rows, counters and tally are identical with and without the flag. The batch asks articles_with_stored_mentions once per flush (one statement, not one per article) and leaves the flag off for an article whose id still carries rows (an id handed out again over rows a tool with foreign keys off left behind: the flag alone would have kept a disjoint keyword's row on the new article), which is read and healed as before. Pinned by the tests incl. the id-reuse proof and the orphan case through the real batch; mutants killed.
